destination.name: Robe
destination.tagline: A historic port town on Guichen Bay with long beaches, dunes and lakes nearby
destination.description: Robe is a coastal town on Guichen Bay on the Limestone Coast, about 340 km from Adelaide. Founded in 1846, it became South Australia's second-busiest port in the 1850s, and more than 16,000 Chinese gold seekers landed here and walked about 320 km to the Victorian goldfields. That past survives in its 1863 customs house and the cliff-top obelisk, while Long Beach and Little Dip Conservation Park cover surf, dunes and lakes to the south. Rock lobster is a mainstay of the local fishing industry.
whyVisit: Swim and surf long ocean beaches

goodToKnow.title: Book campsites ahead
goodToKnow.detail: Little Dip's campsites must be booked before arrival, up to 12 months ahead. Vehicle entry to the park is free.

goodToKnow.title: Check beach driving
goodToKnow.detail: Cars are allowed on Long Beach's firm sand, mainly in summer. Check tide and sand conditions before driving on.

destination.name: Beachport
destination.tagline: A Rivoli Bay town with a long jetty, a floating salt lake and wild coastal parks
destination.description: Beachport is a small town on Rivoli Bay on the Limestone Coast, about 385 km from Adelaide. An 1879 wool and grain store beside the old railway line is now a National Trust museum, and a long jetty reaches out over the bay. Around the town, a salt lake for floating, limestone cliffs in Beachport Conservation Park and the surf beaches and dunes of Canunda National Park fill a day or two.
whyVisit: Walk limestone cliffs and coastal trails
Stroll out on a historic jetty

goodToKnow.title: Book park campsites
goodToKnow.detail: Campsites in the nearby parks must be booked before arrival, from $19.80 a night. Vehicle entry to each is free.

goodToKnow.title: Swim at the pool

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Calm, warm days from {months} suit a float in the Pool of Siloam and walks along the clifftops.
